comments.value: The idea of friends only is for ONLY FRIENDS of their VRChat account to join. If they are avoiding a player, they can either block them temporarily, or unfriend them. If they want a particular user to join, they will invite them. If they want more flexibility then they can drop a portal to a new instance.

details:
TL:DR: Even the owner cannot invite non-friends to their own don't-trust-their-friends world, and there should be some flexibility since they're the owner.  Maybe they're just avoiding certain disruptive people, but would let others in on an individual basis.  Not possible, now.

Invite-only and invite+ are already pretty anti-social, but at least they're impersonal about it and aren't completely rigid.  The owner wants some control over who enters, and decides that either they alone can invite or those they invite can invite.  Requesting invites is also possible.  It's controlled, but flexible.

Friends worlds offer slightly less security but are much more flexible.  Anyone who joins must be a friend of the owner, or a friend of a friend of the owner, and so on.  It's like an auto-vouching system.  If they can get in, they were a friend of someone.  If they cause a problem, it can be dealt with on an individual basis.  Which, with everyone being friends on some level, shouldn't be much of a problem.

Friends-only worlds not only add control on a weirdly personal level, with the owner declaring that only his direct friends may visit and these friends cannot vouch for their friends (and so on), but it actually prevents the guests AND the owner from receving invite requests from or sending invites to anyone else.  Only direct friends of the guest may enter, period.  It might as well be called "don't trust your own friends."

Which to an extent makes some sense, since their friends might be friends with troublemakers, and they might not want someone who is particularly disruptive.  However, should they actually be okay with their friends' friends, maybe it's just a few specific users they want to keep out, this mode offers them no flexibility.  The room owner cannot receive requests from or send invites to non-friends, even if he wants to let them in.

So, yeah.  Not only is friends-only anti-social in this social game, but it goes beyond that and offers no flexibility to the room owner.  It's like invite-only, but worse.  It also encourages friend request spamming, which I may have to resort to soon because I want to join my friend but I've been avoiding friending his friends since I'd like to be, you know, friends first.  But some of them insist on using friends-only, and the only other way in is for them to remake.

This could be fixed by simply allowing the owner to accept invite requests from and send invites to non-friends.  In the case of requests, these could be made by non-friends clicking request invite through their friends who are already in.  Joining would still only be possible for direct friends of the owner.

Alternatively, this could be fixed by allowing owners to change room settings without remaking, something that has probably been suggested, and should be implemented regardless.  However, swapping room settings from and to friends-only to let someone in seems less convenient than simply having the option to respond to requests or invite.

Either option makes more sense than a setting that doesn't even give the owner the option to allow non-friends on an individual basis.
title: friends-only worlds are glaringly anti-social, need flexibility
